label: RITVAYA • DAILY RHYTHM
caption:
Most people meet Dinacharya as a long morning list: tongue scraping, oil pulling, oil massage, meditation, yoga, warm water… and it lasts about a week.

But Dinacharya simply means "daily conduct." In the Ashtanga Hridaya, it's a sequence that follows the day's natural rhythm:
→ Morning (Kapha time): the body feels heavy, so wake early and move.
→ Midday (Pitta time): digestion is strongest, so eat your main meal.
→ Evening (Kapha again): the body slows down, so wind down and sleep by about 10.

What modern research adds:
• Regular sleep and wake times, morning light, and consistent meals support your body's circadian clock.
• Tongue scraping can modestly reduce tongue coating and bad breath.
• Oil pulling has limited evidence. It's an extra, never a replacement for brushing.

So don't start with 20 steps. Start with three anchors, then add one practice at a time once they feel automatic.

Start with this today: pick one anchor and keep it for 3 days. Observe what changes.

💬 Which anchor is hardest for you: waking, midday meal, or sleeping on time?

Educational content, not medical advice. If you work night shifts or have a health condition, adapt the timings with your doctor.
